lessons.title: Both … and: Connecting Two Items
lessons.content: 'Both … and' is used to refer to two things or people together. It connects two nouns, adjectives, or phrases of the same grammatical type. The structure is 'Both + noun/adjective + and + noun/adjective'.

details.explanation: Use 'both … and' to join two nouns that share the same action or quality.
details.example: Both Alice and Susan have to comply with the rules.
details.burmese: Both Alice and Susan have to comply with the rules.

details.explanation: Use 'both … and' to join two adjectives describing the same subject.
details.example: Sue is both kind and helpful to others.
details.burmese: Sue is both kind and helpful to others.

details.explanation: When 'both … and' connects two subjects, the verb is always plural.
details.example: Both the students and the teacher are in the class.
details.burmese: Both the students and the teacher are in the class.

lessons.title: Subject-Verb Agreement with Both … and
lessons.content: When 'both … and' joins two subjects, the verb is always plural, even if one subject is singular. This is because 'both' implies two things together, which is always treated as plural.

details.explanation: Even if one subject is singular, use a plural verb when joining with 'both … and'.
details.example: Both Tom and Ann were late.
details.burmese: Both Tom and Ann were late.

details.explanation: In negative sentences, 'both … and' uses the plural negative form.
details.example: Both Daniel and Kim don't drink tea.
details.burmese: Both Daniel and Kim don't drink tea.
